headline: Medium prompt-injection and data-leakage risk: Khoj ingests personal notes/files while the paired awesome-list has no runtime surface, so interaction risk is mostly one-way and docs-only.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A has no runtime I/O surfaces and is not runnable, so it cannot ingest B directly. B reads indexed files and supports chat/RAG, so if A’s content is manually copied into Khoj or indexed there, prompt-like content could influence responses. The pathway is indirect and requires unusual bridging, so low is appropriate.
conditions: IF A’s repository content is manually pasted into B’s chat or indexed documents
IF B treats retrieved file text as instruction-like content without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable indexing of untrusted notes for the session
Use a separate workspace for imported content
Add a prefix banner marking retrieved text as untrusted
Review retrieved snippets before acting on them

B_data_leakage.rationale: B reads personal notes/files and can call APIs or configured search providers, so sensitive content may flow outward in default use. A has no data classes touched and no egress, so it does not add leakage risk itself. Because B’s default retrieval plus external calls can expose indexed content, the pair’s leakage risk is medium.
conditions: IF B indexes personal notes containing secrets or private documents
IF B is configured to use cloud APIs or external search providers
mitigations: Restrict B to local/self-hosted providers
Exclude secret-bearing folders from indexing
Rotate any exposed API keys after import
Turn off external search for sensitive sessions
Audit recent retrieved documents before sharing outputs

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has no write or network capabilities and is not runnable, while B cannot write files or modify git state. There is no overlapping mutable resource in the profiles, so direct capability conflict is limited to read-side contention over B’s indexed documents. That makes the blast radius small and the severity low.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same indexed document set
IF B’s shared index is updated concurrently by multiple clients
mitigations: Stagger indexing jobs
Use separate document collections per workflow
Freeze the index during critical review
Avoid concurrent edits to source notes

D_cascading_error.rationale: B’s retrieval/chat workflow can treat indexed text as authoritative, and A is a curated list that may be used as source material. If A’s recommendations are imported into B, B may surface them without verification. A does not act, but B can amplify unverified content, so the cascade is plausible in default use and medium severity fits.
conditions: IF A’s list entries are imported into B as reference material
IF B answers from retrieved snippets without a human verification step
mitigations: Require citation review before acting on answers
Mark imported list entries as non-authoritative
Use a verification checklist for retrieved claims
Limit B to summarization rather than action-taking

E_compliance.rationale: B explicitly touches personal notes and indexed documents and may send them to Khoj cloud or configured search providers, creating a residency/retention mismatch risk. A has no touched data classes and no egress, so it is not the compliance driver. The pair therefore inherits B’s compliance exposure, but the evidence does not show a specific regulated class, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF indexed documents include regulated personal data
IF B is connected to a cloud or third-party search provider with different retention rules
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of indexed folders
Use self-hosted endpoints only
Document retention settings before import
Purge sensitive documents from the index after use
